title: Consumer equilibrium and how price and income changes move it
summary: Equilibrium where MRS = Px/Py, substitutes and complements, normal and inferior goods, with the slides' examples.

chunks.heading: Consumer equilibrium
chunks.explanation_md:
The **equilibrium consumption bundle** is the **affordable bundle that yields the highest level of satisfaction**.

It occurs where **MRS = Px / Py**. Equivalently, the **slope of the indifference curve equals the slope of the budget line**. On the graph the budget line just touches the highest reachable indifference curve (among I, II and III), with intercepts M/Py and M/Px.

Think of it this way: the consumer's willingness to swap (MRS) matches the market's rate of swapping (Px/Py).

key_terms.meaning: The affordable bundle that gives the highest satisfaction, where MRS = Px/Py.

chunks.exam_line: Equilibrium: the affordable bundle with the highest satisfaction, where MRS = Px/Py (indifference curve slope equals budget line slope).

chunks.heading: Price changes: substitutes and complements
chunks.explanation_md:
**Substitute goods:** an increase (decrease) in the price of X leads to an **increase (decrease)** in consumption of Y. Examples: **Coke and Pepsi**; **Verizon Wireless or AT&T**.

**Complementary goods:** an increase (decrease) in the price of X leads to a **decrease (increase)** in consumption of Y. Examples: **DVD and DVD players**; **computer CPUs and monitors**.

**The graph:** Beer is X, pretzels are Y. When the price of beer falls (Px1 > Px2) and consumption of pretzels **rises** from Y1 to Y2, X and Y are **complements**. The consumer moves from bundle A to bundle B on a higher curve (II instead of I).

key_terms.meaning: A rise (fall) in the price of X raises (lowers) consumption of Y.
A rise (fall) in the price of X lowers (raises) consumption of Y.

chunks.heading: Income changes: normal and inferior goods
chunks.explanation_md:
**Normal good:** an increase (decrease) in income leads to an **increase (decrease)** in its consumption.

**Inferior good:** an increase (decrease) in income leads to a **decrease (increase)** in its consumption.

The graph for normal goods shows income rising from M0 to M1 (M0 < M1): the budget line shifts out and the consumer moves from bundle A to bundle B on a higher curve, with more of good X (X0 to X1) and more of Y (Y0 to Y1).
chunks.exam_line: Normal good: income up, consumption up. Inferior good: income up, consumption down.

questions.model_answer_md:
The equilibrium bundle is the **affordable bundle that yields the highest level of satisfaction**.

Condition: **MRS = Px / Py**, or equivalently the **slope of the indifference curve equals the slope of the budget line**.

In words, the rate at which the consumer is willing to swap goods equals the rate at which the market lets her swap.

questions.stem: In the pretzels and beer graph the price of beer falls and pretzel consumption rises. What does this show and how is it drawn?
questions.model_answer_md:
Beer is good X on the horizontal axis and pretzels are good Y on the vertical axis. When the price of beer falls (Px1 > Px2), the consumer moves from bundle A to bundle B, on a higher curve, and consumption of pretzels rises from Y1 to Y2.

Because the price of X fell and consumption of Y rose, **X and Y are complements**.

questions.stem: Explain consumer equilibrium and how it is affected by changes in the price of a related good and by changes in income.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Introduction.** The consumer picks the affordable bundle that gives the highest satisfaction.

**Equilibrium.** MRS = Px / Py: the indifference curve and budget line have the same slope.

**Price of a related good.** If an increase in the price of X raises consumption of Y, the goods are substitutes (Coke and Pepsi). If it lowers consumption of Y, they are complements (DVD and DVD players).

**Income.** Normal goods: consumption rises with income. Inferior goods: consumption falls as income rises.

**Conclusion.** The direction of change in consumption classifies the goods.

questions.stem: Using the graph of bundles A and B after the price of beer falls, explain how the consumer reaches a new equilibrium and what the diagram tells us about beer and pretzels.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Introduction.** A price fall changes the budget line and the consumer's best bundle.

**Set up.** Pretzels (Y) are on the vertical axis, beer (X) on the horizontal. The intercepts are M/Py for pretzels and M/Px1 and M/Px2 for beer.

**Movement.** Price of beer falls (Px1 > Px2): the budget line rotates out and the consumer moves from A (X1, Y1) on curve I to B (X2, Y2) on curve II.

**Interpretation.** Pretzel consumption rises from Y1 to Y2 as the price of beer falls, so beer and pretzels are complements. Equilibrium is again where MRS = Px/Py.

**Conclusion.** The graph is the slides' illustration of complementary goods.
